sourceSentences.text: ‘Oh, damn it all.
I didn’t mean to be seen like this,’ Chade breathed.
I watched his pale hands gather his reins, turning his bay.
‘Follow me, boy.’
He did not look toward the man who still pointed a quavering finger at us.
He moved slowly, almost languorously, as he guided his horse off the road and up a tussocky hillside.
It was the same unchallenging way of moving that Burrich had when confronting a wary horse or dog.
His tired horse left the smooth trail reluctantly.
Chade was headed up into a stand of birches on the hilltop.
I stared at him uncomprehendingly.
‘Follow me, boy,’ he directed me over his shoulder when I hesitated.
‘Do you want to be stoned in the road?
It’s not a pleasant experience.’
I moved carefully, swinging Sooty aside from the road as if I were totally unaware of the panicky folk ahead of us.
They hovered there, between anger and fear.
The feel of it was a black-red smear on the day’s freshness.
I saw a woman stoop, saw a man turn aside from his barrow.
‘They’re coming!’
I warned Chade, even as they raced toward us.
Some gripped stones, and others green staffs freshly taken from the forest.
All had the bedraggled look of townsfolk forced to live in the open.
Here were the rest of Forge’s villagers, those not taken hostage by the Raiders.
All of that I realized in the instant between digging in my heels and Sooty’s weary plunge forward.
Our horses were spent; their efforts at speed were grudging, despite the hail of rocks that thudded to the earth in our wake.
Had the townsfolk been rested, or less fearful, they would have easily caught us.
But I think they were relieved to see us flee.
Their minds were more fixed on what walked the streets of their village than in fleeing strangers, no matter how ominous.
They stood in the road and shouted and waved their sticks until we were among the trees.
Chade had taken the lead and I didn’t question him as he took us on a parallel path that would keep us out of the sight of the folk leaving Forge.
The horses had settled back into a grudging plod.
I was grateful for the rolling hills and scattered trees that hid us from any pursuit.
When I saw a stream glinting, I gestured to it without a word.
Silently we watered the horses, and shook out for them some grain from Chade’s supplies.
I loosened harness, and wiped their draggled coats with handfuls of grass.
For ourselves, there was cold streamwater and coarse travel-bread.
I saw to the horses as best as I could.
Chade seemed full of his own thoughts, and for a long time I respected their intensity.
But finally I could contain my curiosity no longer and I asked the question.
‘Are you really the Pocked Man?’
Chade startled, and then stared at me.
There were equal parts amazement and ruefulness in that look.
‘The Pocked Man?
The legendary harbinger of disease and disaster?
Oh, come, boy, you’re not simple.
That legend is hundreds of years old.
Surely you can’t believe I’m that ancient.’
I shrugged.
I wanted to say, ‘You are scarred, and you bring death’, but I did not utter it.
Chade did seem very old to me sometimes, and other times so full of energy that he seemed but a very young man in an old man’s body.
‘No, I am not the Pocked Man,’ he went on, more to himself than to me.
‘But after today, the rumours of him will be spread across the Six Duchies like pollen on the wind.
There will be talk of disease and pestilence and divine punishments for imagined wrongdoing.
I wish I had not been seen like this.
The folk of the kingdom already have enough to fear.
But there are sharper worries for us than superstitions.
However you knew it, you were right.
I have been thinking, most carefully, of everything I saw in Forge.
And recalling the words of those villagers who tried to stone us.
And the look of them all.
I knew the Forge folk, in times past.
They were doughty folk, not the type to flee in superstitious panic.
But those folk we saw on the road, that was what they were doing.
Leaving Forge, forever, or at least so they intend.
Taking all that is left that they can carry.
Leaving homes their grandfathers were born in.
And leaving behind relatives who sift and scavenge in the ruins like witlings.

paragraphPairs.sourceText: ‘They’re coming!’ I warned Chade, even as they raced toward us. Some gripped stones, and others green staffs freshly taken from the forest. All had the bedraggled look of townsfolk forced to live in the open. Here were the rest of Forge’s villagers, those not taken hostage by the Raiders. All of that I realized in the instant between digging in my heels and Sooty’s weary plunge forward. Our horses were spent; their efforts at speed were grudging, despite the hail of rocks that thudded to the earth in our wake. Had the townsfolk been rested, or less fearful, they would have easily caught us. But I think they were relieved to see us flee. Their minds were more fixed on what walked the streets of their village than in fleeing strangers, no matter how ominous.

paragraphPairs.sourceText: They stood in the road and shouted and waved their sticks until we were among the trees. Chade had taken the lead and I didn’t question him as he took us on a parallel path that would keep us out of the sight of the folk leaving Forge. The horses had settled back into a grudging plod. I was grateful for the rolling hills and scattered trees that hid us from any pursuit. When I saw a stream glinting, I gestured to it without a word. Silently we watered the horses, and shook out for them some grain from Chade’s supplies. I loosened harness, and wiped their draggled coats with handfuls of grass. For ourselves, there was cold streamwater and coarse travel-bread. I saw to the horses as best as I could. Chade seemed full of his own thoughts, and for a long time I respected their intensity. But finally I could contain my curiosity no longer and I asked the question.

Чейд ехал впереди, и я не стал его расспрашивать, когда он повёл нас параллельной тропой, которая не позволяла людям, покидавшим Кузницу, нас заметить. Лошади вновь перешли на неохотную трусцу. Я был благодарен холмистой местности и редким деревьям, скрывавшим нас от любого преследования. Увидев блеснувший ручей, я молча указал на него. Мы молча напоили лошадей и вытряхнули для них немного зерна из припасов Чейда. Я ослабил сбрую и протёр их свалявшуюся шерсть пучками травы. Нам достались холодная вода из ручья и грубый дорожный хлеб. Я позаботился о лошадях как мог. Чейд, казалось, был поглощён собственными мыслями, и долгое время я уважал их напряжённость. Но наконец я не смог больше сдерживать любопытство и задал вопрос.

paragraphPairs.sourceText: ‘No, I am not the Pocked Man,’ he went on, more to himself than to me. ‘But after today, the rumours of him will be spread across the Six Duchies like pollen on the wind. There will be talk of disease and pestilence and divine punishments for imagined wrongdoing. I wish I had not been seen like this. The folk of the kingdom already have enough to fear. But there are sharper worries for us than superstitions. However you knew it, you were right. I have been thinking, most carefully, of everything I saw in Forge. And recalling the words of those villagers who tried to stone us. And the look of them all. I knew the Forge folk, in times past. They were doughty folk, not the type to flee in superstitious panic. But those folk we saw on the road, that was what they were doing. Leaving Forge, forever, or at least so they intend. Taking all that is left that they can carry. Leaving homes their grandfathers were born in. And leaving behind relatives who sift and scavenge in the ruins like witlings.
paragraphPairs.translatedText: — Нет, я не Рябой Человек, — продолжил он, скорее для себя, чем для меня. — Но после сегодняшнего дня слухи о нём разлетятся по Шести Герцогствам, как пыльца по ветру. Заговорят о болезнях, мору и божественных карах за воображаемые прегрешения. Жаль, что меня увидели таким. Людям королевства и без того есть чего бояться. Но для нас есть заботы острее суеверий. Как бы ты ни узнал, ты оказался прав. Я очень тщательно обдумывал всё, что увидел в Кузнице. И вспоминал слова тех жителей, которые пытались забросать нас камнями. И выражение лиц всех их. В прежние времена я знал людей Кузницы. Это были стойкие люди, не из тех, кто бежит в суеверной панике. Но люди, которых мы видели на дороге, именно это и делали. Покидали Кузницу навсегда — или, по крайней мере, таково их намерение. Уносили всё, что осталось и что они могли нести. Бросали дома, в которых родились их деды. mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: When I saw a stream glinting, I gestured to it without a word.

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: Silently we watered the horses, and shook out for them some grain from Chade’s supplies.

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: I loosened harness, and wiped their draggled coats with handfuls of grass.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.targetText: Я ослабил сбрую и протёр их свалявшуюся шерсть пучками травы.

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: For ourselves, there was cold streamwater and coarse travel-bread.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: For ourselves, there was cold streamwater and coarse travel-bread.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.targetText: Нам достались холодная вода из ручья и грубый дорожный хлеб.

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: I saw to the horses as best as I could.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: I saw to the horses as best as I could.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.targetText: Я позаботился о лошадях как мог.

mappedSourceRanges.text: I saw to the horses as best as I could.

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: Chade seemed full of his own thoughts, and for a long time I respected their intensity.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: Chade seemed full of his own thoughts, and for a long time I respected their intensity.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.targetText: Чейд, казалось, был поглощён собственными мыслями, и долгое время я уважал их напряжённость.

mappedSourceRanges.text: Chade seemed full of his own thoughts, and for a long time I respected their intensity.

targetRanges.text: Чейд, казалось, был поглощён собственными мыслями, и долгое время я уважал их напряжённость.

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: But finally I could contain my curiosity no longer and I asked the question.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: But finally I could contain my curiosity no longer and I asked the question.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.targetText: Но наконец я не смог больше сдерживать любопытство и задал вопрос.

mappedSourceRanges.text: But finally I could contain my curiosity no longer and I asked the question.

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: ‘Are you really the Pocked Man?’
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: ‘Are you really the Pocked Man?’
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.targetText: — Ты и вправду Рябой Человек?

sourceRanges.text: ‘Are you really the Pocked Man?’

mappedSourceRanges.text: ‘Are you really the Pocked Man?’

targetRanges.text: — Ты и вправду Рябой Человек?

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: Chade startled, and then stared at me.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: Chade startled, and then stared at me.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.targetText: Чейд вздрогнул, а потом уставился на меня.

mappedSourceRanges.text: Chade startled, and then stared at me.

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: There were equal parts amazement and ruefulness in that look.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: There were equal parts amazement and ruefulness in that look.

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: ‘The Pocked Man?
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: ‘The Pocked Man?
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.targetText: — Рябой Человек?

sourceRanges.text: ‘The Pocked Man?

mappedSourceRanges.text: ‘The Pocked Man?

targetRanges.text: — Рябой Человек?

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: The legendary harbinger of disease and disaster?
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: The legendary harbinger of disease and disaster?
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.targetText: Легендарный предвестник болезней и бедствий?

sourceRanges.text: The legendary harbinger of disease and disaster?

mappedSourceRanges.text: The legendary harbinger of disease and disaster?

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: Oh, come, boy, you’re not simple.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: Oh, come, boy, you’re not simple.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.targetText: Да брось, мальчик, ты же не простак.

sourceRanges.text: Oh, come, boy, you’re not simple.

mappedSourceRanges.text: Oh, come, boy, you’re not simple.

targetRanges.text: Да брось, мальчик, ты же не простак.

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: That legend is hundreds of years old.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: That legend is hundreds of years old.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.targetText: Этой легенде сотни лет.

sourceRanges.text: That legend is hundreds of years old.

mappedSourceRanges.text: That legend is hundreds of years old.

targetRanges.text: Этой легенде сотни лет.

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: Surely you can’t believe I’m that ancient.’
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: Surely you can’t believe I’m that ancient.’
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.targetText: Неужели ты можешь верить, что я настолько древний?

mappedSourceRanges.text: Surely you can’t believe I’m that ancient.’

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: I shrugged.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: I shrugged.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.targetText: Я пожал плечами.

sourceRanges.text: I shrugged.

mappedSourceRanges.text: I shrugged.

targetRanges.text: Я пожал плечами.

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: I wanted to say, ‘You are scarred, and you bring death’, but I did not utter it.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: I wanted to say, ‘You are scarred, and you bring death’, but I did not utter it.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.targetText: Я хотел сказать: «Ты весь в шрамах и несёшь смерть», — но не произнёс этого.

mappedSourceRanges.text: I wanted to say, ‘You are scarred, and you bring death’, but I did not utter it.

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: Chade did seem very old to me sometimes, and other times so full of energy that he seemed but a very young man in an old man’s body.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: Chade did seem very old to me sometimes, and other times so full of energy that he seemed but a very young man in an old man’s body.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.targetText: Иногда Чейд казался мне очень старым, а иногда таким полным сил, что представлялся совсем молодым человеком в теле старика.

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: ‘No, I am not the Pocked Man,’ he went on, more to himself than to me.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: ‘No, I am not the Pocked Man,’ he went on, more to himself than to me.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.targetText: — Нет, я не Рябой Человек, — продолжил он, скорее для себя, чем для меня.

sourceRanges.text: ‘No, I am not the Pocked Man,’ he went on, more to himself than to me.

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: ‘But after today, the rumours of him will be spread across the Six Duchies like pollen on the wind.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: ‘But after today, the rumours of him will be spread across the Six Duchies like pollen on the wind.

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: There will be talk of disease and pestilence and divine punishments for imagined wrongdoing.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: There will be talk of disease and pestilence and divine punishments for imagined wrongdoing.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.targetText: Заговорят о болезнях, мору и божественных карах за воображаемые прегрешения.

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: I wish I had not been seen like this.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: I wish I had not been seen like this.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.targetText: Жаль, что меня увидели таким.

sourceRanges.text: I wish I had not been seen like this.

mappedSourceRanges.text: I wish I had not been seen like this.

targetRanges.text: Жаль, что меня увидели таким.

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: The folk of the kingdom already have enough to fear.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: The folk of the kingdom already have enough to fear.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.targetText: Людям королевства и без того есть чего бояться.

sourceRanges.text: The folk of the kingdom already have enough to fear.

mappedSourceRanges.text: The folk of the kingdom already have enough to fear.

targetRanges.text: Людям королевства и без того есть чего бояться.

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: But there are sharper worries for us than superstitions.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: But there are sharper worries for us than superstitions.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.targetText: Но для нас есть заботы острее суеверий.

sourceRanges.text: But there are sharper worries for us than superstitions.

mappedSourceRanges.text: But there are sharper worries for us than superstitions.

targetRanges.text: Но для нас есть заботы острее суеверий.

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: However you knew it, you were right.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: However you knew it, you were right.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.targetText: Как бы ты ни узнал, ты оказался прав.

sourceRanges.text: However you knew it, you were right.

mappedSourceRanges.text: However you knew it, you were right.

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: I have been thinking, most carefully, of everything I saw in Forge.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: I have been thinking, most carefully, of everything I saw in Forge.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.targetText: Я очень тщательно обдумывал всё, что увидел в Кузнице.

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: And recalling the words of those villagers who tried to stone us.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: And recalling the words of those villagers who tried to stone us.

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: And the look of them all.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: And the look of them all.

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: I knew the Forge folk, in times past.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: I knew the Forge folk, in times past.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.targetText: В прежние времена я знал людей Кузницы.

mappedSourceRanges.text: I knew the Forge folk, in times past.

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: They were doughty folk, not the type to flee in superstitious panic.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: They were doughty folk, not the type to flee in superstitious panic.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.targetText: Это были стойкие люди, не из тех, кто бежит в суеверной панике.

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: But those folk we saw on the road, that was what they were doing.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: But those folk we saw on the road, that was what they were doing.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.targetText: Но люди, которых мы видели на дороге, именно это и делали.

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: Leaving Forge, forever, or at least so they intend.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: Leaving Forge, forever, or at least so they intend.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.targetText: Покидали Кузницу навсегда — или, по крайней мере, таково их намерение.

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: Taking all that is left that they can carry.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: Taking all that is left that they can carry.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.targetText: Уносили всё, что осталось и что они могли нести.

mappedSourceRanges.text: Taking all that is left that they can carry.

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: Leaving homes their grandfathers were born in.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: Leaving homes their grandfathers were born in.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.targetText: Бросали дома, в которых родились их деды.

mappedSourceRanges.text: Leaving homes their grandfathers were born in.

mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.sourceText: And leaving behind relatives who sift and scavenge in the ruins like witlings.
mappedSentenceGroupAlignments.mappedSourceText: And leaving behind relatives who sift and scavenge in the ruins like witlings.
